A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Trust-Region Twisted Policy Improvement. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TRT-SMC experiments on discrete and continuous environments, policy-estimation simulations, and component ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds trust-region sensitivity results and an analysis accounting for planning samples.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Algorithm 2 change the ancestor-value increment from (1/n) log(sum r_i) to log((1/n) sum r_i), where n counts descendants and r_i are incremental importance-weight ratios. This changes the prescribed policy-inference calculation locally; the PDFs do not establish whether executed code changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use Jumanji Snake and Rubikscube, Brax Ant and Halfcheetah, and the zero-reward toy environment described in Appendix B.6. The added analyses introduce no new environments or task requirements.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain variational SMC, Gumbel MCTS, PPO, A2C for Jumanji, and SAC for Brax. The component comparators also remain unchanged. Revised A2C curves do not constitute a new comparison method.

E3.justification: The new sensitivity experiment evaluates alpha values 0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.8 at budgets 16, 64, and 256 with K=m. Figure 8 additionally counts planning transitions in sample efficiency. Previously reported main evaluation settings, including 128 evaluation episodes, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 extends the existing proposal ablations with a broader alpha-sensitivity analysis, aggregated in Figure 5 and separated into discrete and continuous domains in Figure 9. Appendix D adds sensitivity to planning-sample accounting through Figure 8. Existing policy-inference, value-target, resampling, and fixed-temperature analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 adds uncertainty bands to A2C curves and removes v1's explicit explanation that A2C lacked intervals because only three seeds were reported. The general 30-seed, 99% BCa-bootstrap convention remains, but an A2C-specific increase in runs is not explicitly documented.

E6.justification: Figure 2 replaces the A2C curves: Snake returns at 20 million samples rise from approximately 30 in v1 to 42 in v3. Figures 5 and 9 add findings about deterioration at high alpha and differing domain sensitivity. Figure 8 reports model-free sample-efficiency advantages under planning-inclusive accounting and displays longer baseline trajectories. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting planner gains; Table 1 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Moving descendant-count normalization inside the logarithm in Section 3.3 and Algorithm 2 is an algebraically substantive estimator correction. Theorem 2.2, Corollary 2.3, and the Appendix A proofs remain unchanged. Shortened Equations 2–3 otherwise restate existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about tailoring SMC through constrained proposals, terminal-state handling, and improved policy/value estimation, with runtime and sample-efficiency benefits over SMC and MCTS.

C2.justification: v1 already warned that model-free comparisons excluded planning transitions. v3 explicitly conditions Figure 2's interpretation on accurate-simulator access and explains the opposing total-sample comparison in Figure 8. It also adds environment-dependent interpretation of alpha sensitivity and the benefit of intermediate prior/value weighting.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces the promise of releasing code and a container upon publication with a statement identifying an available code repository. This improves access information within the PDF; repository availability was not independently checked. Hardware, architecture descriptions, software versions, and existing hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gu et al. (2015), Neural Adaptive Sequential Monte Carlo, to the variational-SMC background and Ziebart (2010) to the maximum-entropy discussion. These are limited citation additions; the substantive positioning against prior SMC and MCTS research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the experimental setup and proposal-ablation discussion, shorter background equation displays, and an updated publication footer. Most prose and the ordering of the main sections and Appendices A–D remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds sensitivity displays in Figures 5 and 9 and the planning-adjusted Figure 8. Figure 2 changes A2C styling and uncertainty bands and extends the Rubikscube vertical axis. Table 1 moves to page 9. v1's appendix Figures 5–6 are retained as v3's Figures 6–7; the overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: v3 consistently corrects the stated estimator in Section 3.3 and Algorithm 2, adds useful evidence about parameter sensitivity and planning-inclusive sample costs, and provides concrete code-access information. These improve correctness and interpretation within a largely unchanged study. The unexplained A2C curve replacement and less explicit seed provenance limit the transparency of that particular update.
